framework.name: CARL
framework.one_liner: Takes a completed episode apart into the Context it happened in, the Action taken, the Result that followed and the Learning drawn from it, then forces a fifth question: which governing rule has to change so that the failure class cannot recur.

slots.label: Context
slots.description: The setting and the constraints the actor was operating inside: who they were, what they had, and which rules, markets or structures bounded them. Usually stated, because accounts open with it.

slots.label: Action
slots.description: What was actually done, as concrete steps in order. CARL keeps the actor's own moves separate from the setting so that the two can fail independently.

slots.label: Result
slots.description: What happened as a consequence: the outcome, measured where possible, including outcomes that contradict each other (an operation that worked inside a business that did not).

slots.label: Learning
slots.description: The single-loop lesson: what the actor would do differently next time inside the same setup. Sometimes said out loud in a reflection, often only implied by the tone of the retelling.

slots.label: Systemic rule
slots.description: The double-loop lesson: the governing assumption, policy or structure that has to change so this class of failure cannot happen again. Almost never stated as a rule, and the reason the fifth slot exists.

relations.label: motivates
relations.description: the context, or an earlier step, motivates what is done next

relations.label: produces
relations.description: an action, or an earlier outcome, produces what happened next

relations.label: constrains
relations.description: a context condition bounds what an action can achieve, up to preventing it outright

relations.label: teaches
relations.description: a result teaches a lesson to the actor

relations.label: generalizes to
relations.description: a lesson, or an observed recurrence, generalises into a standing rule

examples.title: A medication near miss on a ward (reflective account)
examples.summary: The reflective-practice setting CARL was written for: a nurse writes up a near miss, draws the obvious lesson about her own care, and the ward then changes something she never proposed. The graph separates the stated account from the two inferences that turn a personal resolution into a systemic rule.

insights.short: Given a ward nurse's reflective account of a near miss in which she drew up 10 mg of morphine instead of 1 mg from look-alike ampoules kept in one drawer and was stopped by an agency nurse's check, applying CARL we derived that the barrier that held was the check, not her care, that vigilance was not what failed once two other nurses had made the same swap, and that the governing rule moves from reading carefully to designing the ambiguity out of storage; what the reader gains is the hidden assumption exposed: reading every label twice holds fixed the arrangement that produced the error.
insights.long:
A second-year ward nurse wrote a reflective account of a late shift as the only registered nurse for sixteen beds, with a healthcare assistant and an agency nurse new to the ward. A patient was prescribed 1 mg of intravenous morphine; she took an ampoule from the controlled-drugs tray, drew up the dose and asked the agency nurse to check it, who read the label back and stopped her: it was 10 mg in 1 ml, not 1 mg. The two strengths sit in the same drawer in almost identical boxes. No morphine reached the patient. Her first lesson was that she had been careless and would read every label twice; the team review a week later found the same swap had happened twice that year to two other nurses, and the ward moved the strengths to separate cupboards with a second signature on the 10 mg ampoule.

CARL asks, after Context, Action, Result and Learning, which governing rule has to change so the failure class cannot recur. The account fills Learning with a single-loop resolution and states the ward's new arrangement, but never names the rule behind the change or says why vigilance was the wrong variable; that gap is where the derived reading sits.

We derived that nothing but the printed strength on a near-identical box separates a dose from ten times that dose (85%); that the error was stopped by a second person reading the label, not by the care taken in drawing the dose up (80%); that because three different nurses made the same mistake, the variable that failed is not individual attention but the arrangement that requires it (85%); and that the governing rule moves from asking people to read more carefully to removing the situation in which a misread is possible at all (80%). No business idea falls out; what the reader gains is the hidden assumption exposed: reading every label twice holds fixed the drawer that made the misread possible, and the rule, once named, transfers to every other look-alike pair on the ward.

source.title: Reflective account written by a second-year ward nurse after a medication near miss
source.text: On a late shift in February I was the only registered nurse covering sixteen beds, working with one healthcare assistant and an agency nurse who had never worked on the ward before. At about nine in the evening a patient was prescribed 1 mg of intravenous morphine for breakthrough pain. I went to the controlled-drugs cupboard, took an ampoule from the tray, drew up the dose, and asked the agency nurse to check it with me before I gave it. She read the label back and stopped me: the ampoule was 10 mg in 1 ml, not 1 mg in 1 ml. The two strengths are kept in the same drawer in almost identical boxes. No morphine reached the patient, and I recorded the event as a near miss before the end of the shift. My first reaction was that I had been careless, and I decided that I would slow down and read every label twice. When the team reviewed the incident the following week, we found that the same two ampoules had been confused twice already that year, by two other nurses. Because it had now happened three times to three different people, the ward changed where the drugs live: the two strengths are stored in separate cupboards and the 10 mg ampoule is released only against a second signature in the controlled-drugs register. I still read every label twice, but I no longer think that is what makes the next dose safe.
source.attribution: Written for this library in the genre CARL is taught in (nursing and allied-health reflective practice); the ward, the shift and the figures are invented, the look-alike-ampoule failure mode is a standard patient-safety case.

edges.rationale: The prescription is what sent her to the cupboard; the account gives the two in sequence without stating the link.
With no second registered nurse on the ward the check could only fall to the agency nurse; the account states the staffing and the request but never connects them.
Taking the wrong strength was possible because both sit in one drawer in almost identical boxes; the arrangement is stated separately from the act.
The catch follows the request to check in the next sentence, but no connective is stated; narrative order is doing the work.
Nothing reaching the patient is the consequence of the ampoule being stopped; the two are reported as separate facts.
The logged near miss is what put the event on the team meeting's agenda; the account states both without joining them.

edges.source_quote: When the team reviewed the incident the following week, we found that the same two ampoules had been confused twice already that year, by two other nurses
My first reaction was that I had been careless, and I decided that I would slow down and read every label twice
Because it had now happened three times to three different people, the ward changed where the drugs live

edges.rationale: Reading the recurrence as evidence about the system rather than about three careless individuals is the inference the ward acted on but the author does not write down.
The single-loop resolution is superseded rather than confirmed once the recurrence is known; the account keeps both without ranking them.
The stated rule change follows from the diagnosis that attention is the wrong variable; the ward states the new arrangement, never the diagnosis.
Once vigilance is ruled out as the failing variable, the only remaining lever is the storage design, which is the governing rule the ward actually changed.

examples.title: Cala: profitable restaurants, terminal structure
examples.summary: Ylan Richard tells the show why Cala, a French food-robotics company with five very profitable restaurants, was shut down two months earlier, and what he is changing in the company he is incorporating now. The operating loop worked and the governing structure did not, which is exactly the situation CARL's fifth slot exists for.

insights.short: Given Ylan Richard's account on TBPN of closing Cala, whose robotic restaurants were profitable with proven payback yet died when Europe's Series A to B funding cliff blocked scaling and French severance law priced the restructure out, applying CARL we derived that no single-loop fix could have saved it, that regulation made a solvable cost problem unsolvable, and that jurisdiction, financing and ownership are design variables chosen at incorporation; the opportunities are a formation tool pricing wind-down cost, and a growth vehicle for proven physical businesses across Europe's A to B gap.
insights.long:
On TBPN on 23 July 2025, Ylan Richard described shutting down Cala, the French company he ran for eight years to make real food more affordable by automating back kitchens with robotics and AI. Results were strong: five very profitable restaurants, sixty per cent weekly retention, ninety-five per cent satisfaction and the only proven return on a whole robotic restaurant. Yet the company hit what he called a gigantic cliff of funding at the European Series A to B moment, French severance law made the restructure cost more cash than it held, and it closed two months earlier. His lessons: the biggest mistake was starting in France; the next company will mix venture with retail private equity, keep HQ lean, consider franchising and open in New York.

CARL separates what was done from what happened and what was learned, then asks which governing rule has to change so the failure cannot recur. Richard fills every slot himself; what he leaves thin is the diagnosis joining them, since he never says why operating lessons could not have saved the old company.

We derived that no single-loop fix could have saved Cala, since every operating measure succeeded while the outcome was terminal (80%); that insolvency protection turned a solvable cost problem into an unsolvable one (80%); that the scaling plan needed capital European venture does not supply (70%); that HQ was sized for the plan, not the five restaurants (70%); that jurisdiction, financing mix and ownership model are design variables to be chosen at incorporation and tested against the wind-down case (75%); and that proven, capital-intensive consumer businesses in Europe have no natural capital source between venture and retail private equity (60%). Opportunity: The formation stack has no tool that prices jurisdiction, severance exposure and wind-down cost at incorporation the way a cap table is modelled, which is the diligence primitive this failure asks for. (75%) Opportunity: A growth vehicle that underwrites unit-economics-proven physical businesses across Europe's Series A to B gap, with retail private-equity discipline and venture speed, addresses a market the speaker describes as a gigantic cliff of funding. (60%)

source.episode_title: Apple Goes Full Throttle on F1, Meme Stocks Make a Comeback, Amazon's New Wearable AI Device (Christina Cacioppo, Deena Shakir, Davide Asnaghi, Ylan Richard)

examples.why_this_episode: A completed eight-year episode told by the founder two months after the shutdown, with the outcome, the mechanism and the lessons all stated out loud, and with a rare property: the actions succeeded on every operating measure the speaker gives while the company still died, so the correction has to happen one loop up. The founder even names the governing assumption that failed, that they did not understand the European financing cliff when they structured the business, which is what CARL's Learning and Systemic rule slots are there to catch.

nodes.label: Robotics to cut restaurant costs
nodes.text: Cala's mission was to make real food more affordable by using robotics and AI to automate back-kitchen operations.
nodes.source_quote: The vision and the mission was to basically make real food more affordable by using robotics and AI to automate the back kitchen operations

nodes.label: Ten million raised from VCs
nodes.text: By the time the first restaurants were working the company had raised ten million dollars from venture investors.
nodes.source_quote: We had raised 10 million up to that point from VCs

nodes.label: European Series A/B cliff
nodes.text: European venture has a structural financing gap at the Series A to Series B moment: a gigantic cliff rather than a next rung.
nodes.source_quote: there's a big financing gap when you get to the Series A slash Series B moment, where basically there's just a gigantic cliff of funding there

nodes.label: French insolvency severance
nodes.text: French law gives employees high severance when a company goes bankrupt, with further state-backed protections on top.
nodes.source_quote: what the regulation actually says is just that when a company goes bankrupt, the employee gets pretty high severance

nodes.label: Cliff unknown at incorporation
nodes.text: The founders did not know about the financing cliff when they created and structured the business.
nodes.source_quote: we did not understand that when we created the business and structured the business

nodes.label: Plan needed capital Europe lacks
nodes.text: The scaling plan required a round of a size European venture does not supply for capital-intensive physical businesses.
nodes.rationale: The speaker states the cliff and states that ten million had been raised just as scaling began; the mismatch between the plan's capital requirement and the market's supply is a reading of those two facts and is never put that way.

nodes.label: Ran the company eight years
nodes.text: The founders ran Cala for eight years, making, in the speaker's words, an ungodly amount of mistakes along the way.
nodes.source_quote: We basically ran the company for eight years, did a bunch, like an ungodly amount of mistakes along the way

nodes.label: Decided to scale on first results
nodes.text: On the strength of the first profitable restaurants the team decided to start scaling.
nodes.source_quote: we have kept those great first results with the restaurants, let's start scaling

nodes.label: Tried to restructure to break even
nodes.text: With scaling blocked, the team tried to restructure away from a handful of profitable restaurants carrying a very high HQ cost.
nodes.source_quote: restructuring the business to go from those hands full of restaurants that were very profitable and a very high HQ cost

nodes.label: Asked regulators for a workaround
nodes.text: The founders went to regulators, the government and any structure around them looking for a workaround.
nodes.source_quote: we basically tried to talk to the regulators, to the government, to any structure that was around us to try and find a workaround

nodes.label: Kept HQ sized for the big plan
nodes.text: Through those years the company carried a headquarters sized for the ambitious plan rather than for the five restaurants it operated.
nodes.rationale: He describes a very high HQ cost against a handful of restaurants and says they had kept a much more ambitious vision than what was achievable in Europe; that the HQ was sized to the plan rather than to the estate is the inference joining those statements.

nodes.label: Five very profitable restaurants
nodes.text: The eight years produced five very, very, very profitable restaurants.
nodes.source_quote: managed to have five very, very, very profitable restaurants

nodes.label: 60% retention, 95% satisfaction
nodes.text: Sixty per cent of customers came back more than once a week and customer satisfaction was ninety-five per cent.
nodes.source_quote: but like 60% retention, customers coming more than once a week, 95% customer satisfaction

nodes.label: Only payback on the robot install
nodes.text: Cala was, with the possible exception of Sweetgreen, the only restaurant business to have proven an incrementally positive return on the whole investment including the machines.
nodes.source_quote: we are the only business that had, and technically Sweetgreen does as well, but had proven, let's say, incrementally positive return investment on the whole investment of a restaurant

nodes.label: Severance liability exceeded cash
nodes.text: The severance liability alone was higher than the cash the company held at the time.
nodes.source_quote: Like the purely the severance liability was higher than the cash on the hands we have at the time

nodes.label: Shut down two months earlier
nodes.text: The business was shut down a bit more than two months before the interview.
nodes.source_quote: we had to shut down the business around a bit more than two months ago

nodes.label: Product worked, scaling did not
nodes.text: The product worked and the economics were there; what the company could not do was keep scaling.
nodes.source_quote: we actually had a product that work and, and the economics were there. We just couldn't keep on scaling

nodes.label: Regulation priced the fix out
nodes.text: Insolvency protection turned a solvable cost problem into an unsolvable one: the cheapest legal route back to profitability cost more cash than the company held.
nodes.rationale: He says the restructuring was possible on paper, that French regulation prevented it, and that the severance liability alone exceeded cash on hand; naming that combination as the failure mechanism joins three separate statements into one.

nodes.label: Mistake was building in France
nodes.text: The biggest mistake was starting the business in Europe, and in France specifically.
nodes.source_quote: the biggest mistakes we made was definitely starting the business in Europe, in France specifically

nodes.label: Should have seen it years earlier
nodes.text: They should have understood two or three years earlier that they could not keep scaling, and been far more conservative in structuring the business.
nodes.source_quote: we should have understood that maybe two or three years earlier and just, uh, been a lot more conservative on the structuring of the business

nodes.label: No single-loop fix could save it
nodes.text: What failed was not how the restaurants were run but how the company was structured, so no improvement inside the existing setup could have changed the outcome.
nodes.rationale: The stated results show the operating loop working (profitable stores, weekly retention, payback on the machines) while the outcome was still terminal; diagnosing the failure as sitting in the governing structure rather than in execution is the double-loop reading the speaker approaches but never states.

nodes.label: Finance with VC and retail PE
nodes.text: The financing strategy has to combine venture capital with private equity that handles retail and restaurants naturally, and the business must be tailored to both.
nodes.source_quote: you have to build a strategy around your financing that's both VC but also private equity that does retail and restaurants more naturally

nodes.label: Keep HQ cost low and lean
nodes.text: The new company keeps a low HQ cost and lean HQ operations, with the other structuring elements changed to match.
nodes.source_quote: that means low HQ cost, more lean HQ operations

nodes.label: Franchise rather than own stores
nodes.text: Franchising is under serious consideration as the path to scale, more aggressively and more capital-efficiently than owning every restaurant as Cala did.
nodes.source_quote: pretty highly considering franchising as kind of a path to scale a lot more aggressively than and a lot more efficiently, capital efficiently than we did with Cali where we own every single restaurant

nodes.label: Next company starts in New York
nodes.text: The roadmap is to launch the first store of the new company in New York around the middle of next year.
nodes.source_quote: The higher level roadmap is to launch the first store in New York, middle of next year

nodes.label: Structure is a design variable
nodes.text: Jurisdiction, financing mix and ownership model are design variables to be chosen at incorporation and tested against the wind-down case, not only against the growth case.
nodes.rationale: Each of the four rules he states changes something that was fixed before the first restaurant opened; the governing rule they share, that structure is chosen and testable rather than inherited from where you happen to live, is the generalisation over them and is what makes the lesson portable.
nodes.idea: The formation stack has no tool that prices jurisdiction, severance exposure and wind-down cost at incorporation the way a cap table is modelled, which is the diligence primitive this failure asks for.

nodes.label: The A/B cliff is an open market
nodes.text: Proven, capital-intensive consumer businesses in Europe have no natural capital source between venture and retail private equity, which is why an operationally successful company had to stop.
nodes.rationale: Generalising one founder's account into a claim about a whole capital market is contestable: the cliff and the financing mix he now prescribes are stated, but the market-level gap and its size are inferred from a single case.
nodes.idea: A growth vehicle that underwrites unit-economics-proven physical businesses across Europe's Series A to B gap, with retail private-equity discipline and venture speed, addresses a market the speaker describes as a gigantic cliff of funding.

edges.rationale: The mission is what the eight years of operating pursued; the speaker states them in sequence rather than as a cause.

edges.source_quote: We basically ran the company for eight years, did a bunch, like an ungodly amount of mistakes along the way, but in the end, managed to have five very, very, very profitable restaurants

edges.rationale: Retention and satisfaction are offered as the numbers behind the profitable restaurants, but the attribution to the eight years of operating is not made in a single span.

edges.source_quote: And so the thinking from there was, okay, we have kept those great first results with the restaurants, let's start scaling
let's start scaling. We had raised 10 million up to that point from VCs and we kind of got hung on a very structural problem of Europe

edges.rationale: He describes hitting the funding wall and then the attempt to restructure to a break-even business; the link is adjacent in the narrative but never stated.

edges.source_quote: We could have cut down cost enough to make the business profitable, but just pure French regulation prevented us from doing that

edges.rationale: The severance liability is what the restructuring ran into; he names the regulation and then the liability in consecutive sentences without joining them.

edges.source_quote: we basically tried to talk to the regulators, to the government, to any structure that was around us to try and find a workaround. But in the end, we couldn't really go beyond what the laws and rules allowed. And so ultimately, we had to shut down the business around a bit more than two months ago

edges.rationale: The liability exceeding cash is why the shutdown was unavoidable, but the two are separated in his account by the attempt to find a workaround.

edges.source_quote: But yeah, in the end, couldn't really get there with Cala. And I think in the end, the biggest mistakes we made was definitely starting the business in Europe, in France specifically

we actually had a product that work and, and the economics were there. We just couldn't keep on scaling and we should have understood that maybe two or three years earlier and just, uh, been a lot more conservative on the structuring of the business

edges.rationale: Being more conservative about structuring is a step towards the diagnosis but stops short of it; naming the governing structure as the thing that failed is the analyst's move.
The new company's first store is in New York; reading that as acting on the France lesson is a link the speaker leaves the listener to make, though he states the two minutes apart.
The financing strategy is offered as the key lesson from the collapse, but the step from being more conservative to combining VC with retail private equity is a generalisation.
A lean HQ is the operational form of being more conservative on structuring; he states both as lessons without connecting them.
Franchising changes the ownership model rather than the operation, which follows from the diagnosis that the operation was not the problem.
If single-loop fixes could not save it, the correction has to be made where the governing variables are set, which is the rule stated at u5.
Turning one company's structural failure into a claim about a missing capital market is the widest step in the graph and the most contestable.
If the plan needed more capital than the market supplies, the decision to scale was already unfundable when it was taken; the speaker states the cliff but not this consequence.
